entries.translation: nao, konyuma, nyuma yake, aho, ahoba; [after this], niko; [in those days], matuku 'galya; [at that time], ijua lyilya; "then" is often expressed by use of the -ka- tense [see Grammar, also condit. tenses].

entries.translation: ngelo, hawa, mbaza, luma, these refer more especially to present time; igeri, ituku, these refer more especially to past time [times], mageri, matuku; [sufficient time], ijua ni ibwaa; [hour], saa; [a long time], luma; [a long time ago], kalere.

entries.english: That one should have / Why one should have (-keja- ... n'ini?)
entries.translation: expressed by inserting -keja- between the pronominal prefix and the verb, followed by the word n'ini?: U-keja-dea hung', n'ini? That you should have done thus, what is it? i.e., why should you have done thus?

entries.english: Ola, ati, atigo, atigoni, ado (Look here! I say!)

entries.translation: usanga. Different kinds: ngange, very small red beads; masamambu, strings of ngange worn as a belt; ngolole, long red beads (kimame); mizigiriro, single strings of ngange; matombo 'ga mbanya, tiny glass beads; maazi, large red beads; magumba, large blue glass beads; mbura, white beads. When made up: kidiri, flat collar; mtungo, bunch of white beads; mkataye, large beads worn by women

entries.english: Cloth (11 trade varieties and 4 linear measures)
entries.translation: nguo. Kinds: mardufu, heavy white; bafta, light white; kaniki, dark blue; birimi, dark blue; isambi, red; barawa, check; kunguru, large check; kitambi, coloured border; leso, handkerchiefs; shuka, loincloth. Measures: mukono (cubit, ~1 1/2 ft), lupande (2 mikono = 1 yard), shuka (4 mikono = 2 yards), doti (8 mikono = 4 yards)

entries.english: Salutation (traditional Taita village, morning, evening, and parting greetings)
entries.translation: On entering a village: Mwaketigwe! Ans. Tsere! — Uvo wenyu? Ans. N'uloli, tili maana! — Morning: Walachile! Ans. N'nalachile! — Evening: Wasindile! Ans. N'nasindile! — Parting: Kala maana! Ans. Genda maana! (Pl. Kalani maana! / Gendani maana!)
entries.pronunciation: mwa-ke-tig-we! tse-re! u-vo we-nyu? wa-la-chi-le! wa-sind-i-le!

entries.english: Seasons (the 4 ecological seasons of the Taita year)
